requirements.note: 1,500 photos, four across with ~2pt gaps, square centre crops, oldest (Feb 19, 2026) at top, opens scrolled to the newest at the bottom, day headings ('Saturday, Oct 24, 2026'). Status-bar tap scrolls to the top; large 'Library' title appears there.

Opens full screen at the photo's aspect ratio with a date/time title and an 'n of 1,500' counter. Swiping left and right both page correctly, it stops at the last photo, and swipe down closes. The image sits a little below centre.
Heart button toggles Favorite/Unfavorite (fills black). A white heart shows on the grid thumbnail straight away.

Albums tab has a 'My Albums' two-column grid of eight albums with rounded covers, names and counts that add up to 1,500. Counts and covers update after deletes. An album opens a day-grouped grid with a back button and Select.

Select turns into Cancel, shows checkmark badges, dims selected photos and counts them ('3 Photos Selected'). Bulk favorite works. Bulk delete asks 'Delete 3 photos?' in an alert, then removes them (1,497).
Favorites and deletions were both still there after relaunch.

bugs: None that break the spec. Hour-of-day labels differ from the other app by 7 hours (e.g. 7:35 PM vs 12:35 PM for the same photo); the day grouping is the same.
tells: Grid cells are announced as Switches (toggle semantics), not as images or buttons: a non-native accessibility tree.
In Select mode the tab bar stays visible. A custom heart / count / trash strip floats above it, and the grid is cut off with a hard edge above that strip. Photos hides the tab bar and uses a toolbar.

At the largest text size the nav bar breaks: the 'Library' title shrinks to the left corner while the '1,497 Photos' subtitle becomes huge. The grid's favorite heart also grows to cover most of a thumbnail.
Delete confirmation is a centred alert, not the action sheet or popover iOS uses for destructive confirmations.
Viewer image is not vertically centred (it sits lower than the space between the bars).
During fast flings a day heading sometimes showed with blank space under it for a frame before its row filled in.
A.scroll: Smooth and momentum-correct over 1,500 photos with no jumps, and the status-bar tap reaches the top. A fast fling sometimes showed a briefly empty row under a heading.

requirements.note: 1,500 photos, four across with thin gaps, square centre crops, oldest at top, opens at the newest. Day headings ('Sunday, October 25') with no year. Native collection view; status-bar tap scrolls to the top.

Opens full screen at the right aspect ratio, swipe left pages forward, swipe down closes. But an ordinary-speed swipe right (1000 pt/s or slower, from mid-screen) closes the viewer back to the grid instead of going to the previous photo. Only a very fast flick (2,500 pt/s) pages backwards. There is no position counter.
Heart toggles Favorite/Unfavorite. A heart.fill badge appears on the grid cell.
Albums is a large-title inset-grouped list: eight rows with a 64pt cover, name, count and chevron. Counts update after deletes. A row pushes a day-grouped album grid with Back and Select.

Select puts '3 Photos Selected' in the title, adds checkmark badges and native selected state. The tab bar gives way to a bottom toolbar with Favorite and Delete. Delete confirms in a native popover ('Delete 3 Photos'). Both actions work.
Favorites and deletions were both still there after relaunch.

bugs: Full-screen viewer: an ordinary swipe right dismisses the viewer instead of showing the previous photo (the interactive dismiss/pop gesture steals the horizontal pan), so going backwards through photos is nearly impossible.
Hour-of-day labels differ from the other app by 7 hours (e.g. 12:35 PM, 1:44 AM). Many photos show small-hours times; the day grouping is the same.
tells: No large title on the Library grid at the top (Photos and the Albums tab both use one).
Day headings are a little cramped (8pt leading inset, compared with the 16pt margins elsewhere).
At the largest text size, album covers stay 64pt next to very large names and counts, which looks unbalanced (nothing truncates).
B.scroll: Native UICollectionView feel: smooth drags, real momentum, rubber-banding, no blank rows or pop-in seen during fast flings, and the status-bar tap reaches the top.

why: B feels more native: a real collection view and inset list, a toolbar that replaces the tab bar in Select mode, a popover delete confirmation, and solid large-text behaviour. But its photo viewer closes when you swipe right at normal speed, which breaks moving backwards between photos, a core part of requirement 2. A meets every requirement cleanly. Its flaws are cosmetic (Switch accessibility, tab bar kept in Select mode, a broken nav bar at the largest text size), so A is the one I would rather ship.
